destinations.title: Must every scalar's self-interactions remain stronger than gravity throughout field space?
Can a local condition on every canonical scalar's self-interactions express gravity being the weakest force, including for massive mediators?

Which scalar mediators can compete with gravity at the cosmological horizon? The proposal includes fields with m_varphi less than or of order H and excludes heavier fields from the horizon-force sum, giving a present-day threshold around 10^-33 eV.

How can scalar couplings be compared with gravity, and can an analogous constraint govern a scalar's self-interactions? The source reviews two conjectural formulations and distinguishes them from repulsive-force criteria preventing bound states.

Do scalar-mediated interactions and scalar self-interactions remain sufficiently strong relative to gravity? The paper distinguishes a state-mass gradient conjecture from a conjecture involving second through fourth derivatives of a self-interaction potential.
Do scalar self-interaction derivatives satisfy the reviewed gravity-comparison inequalities, under the stated canonical-field and mass-identification assumptions?
